title: Keep one customer's quote off another's

blocks.text: The shop's quote service creates one `QuoteFormatter` at startup, and every request thread uses it. Since the last release, support gets a ticket every few days: a customer's PDF quote shows lines or a total that belong to another customer's quote, made at about the same time. Nobody has reproduced it in a test.
Price lookups go to the pricing service and can take seconds, so a quote often stops halfway through while other quotes are rendered.

Write `render(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteFormatter.java`. It returns one line per SKU, in the order given, built with `line(sku, cents)`, then `line("TOTAL", sum)`. When you're done, two quotes rendered at the same time each come out with only their own lines and their own total, and no quote waits for another one's slow price. About eight lines in total.
The tests stop one quote inside a slow price lookup and render another while it waits.

cases.says: a quote has one line per SKU, in order, and a total line with their sum
a quote rendered after another holds only its own lines
a quote rendered on another thread while one is half done leaves the first quote's lines intact
a quote rendered on another thread while one is half done leaves the first quote's total intact
a quote finishes while another quote is waiting for a slow price

origin.section: Fields, Statics and Array Elements Are Shared; Locals and Parameters Are Not

concepts: Fields, statics and array elements are shared between threads while locals and parameters are not, so per-call state kept in a local is safe and the same state kept in a field of a shared object mixes overlapping calls.
